The Data-Type Ontology

data-type-ontology.Rmd

Why a column needs more than a type

A CSV cell like 47401 is just text. Is it a ZIP code, a county FIPS, a count of something? A single “type” label cannot capture that: 47401 and 06037 are both five-digit geographic codes (same type), but one is a ZIP and one is a county (different meaning), and neither should be summed like a number (different treatment). formex pulls these apart onto a small set of coordinates, held in the research data-type ontology — the shared vocabulary that guess_data_type() and fx_stabilize() both speak.

Read the ontology with fx_ontology(); it ships as a diff-able CSV (inst/extdata/research_data_type_ontology_v6.csv) and a parsed data/ontology.rda, and a package test asserts the two agree.

o <- fx_ontology()
dim(o)
#> [1] 96 25

Each row is one format variant of a semantic type. The columns fall into four groups: the path (what a column is), the detection kind (how it is recognized), the recipe (how raw values are stabilized), and metadata (units, validation, lifecycle).

The path: four coordinates

A column is placed on a four-level path, coarse to fine:

data_type  ›  semantic_family  ›  semantic_type  ›  format_label
 treatment      broad role         specific meaning     surface form
  • data_type — how a value is treated: number, text, boolean, temporal, categorical, identifier, structured, unknown.
  • semantic_family — the broad role within a type (e.g. currency, name, date, geographic).
  • semantic_type — the specific meaning that carries the validation and the render treatment (e.g. usd, person, calendar, us_state).
  • format_label — the surface form the file happens to use for that meaning; one semantic type can have several (e.g. an ISBN written 10-digit, 13-digit, or hyphenated). The format_label selects the recipe row.

data_type through semantic_type say what a column is — its intended meaning, stable across file versions. format_label describes how the current file writes it. That is why guess_data_type() can return a path prefix when it is confident about the type but not the exact format: it stops at the deepest coordinate the values actually support.

Every semantic type also carries a stable semantic_type_id (e.g. n0059), and each variant a variant_id (e.g. n0059-f01). Ids are allocated once and never renumbered, so banked test cases and downstream governance files stay valid across ontology versions.

The full hierarchy

Built live from fx_ontology() — data_type › semantic_family : semantic_types:

boolean

  • binary — indicator, mixed, presence, response, status

categorical

  • multiselect — tags
  • mutually_exclusive — classification_code, geographic, missingness_reason, ordered, unordered
  • scale — grade_level, likert, ranking, rating

identifier

  • id — administrative, entity, geographic, hash, record, version

number

  • coordinate — lat, lat_lon, lon, lon_lat
  • currency — balance, euro, usd
  • portion — odds, percent, percentile, probability
  • quantity — count, duration, index, measurement, rank, rate, ratio, score
  • range — confidence_interval, min_max

structured

  • collection — array, list
  • geometry — point, polygon
  • record — key_value, object

temporal

  • date — calendar, timestamp
  • interval — date_range
  • period — month, quarter, reporting_period, year
  • phase — day_of_week, hour_of_day, month_of_year, week_of_year
  • time — clock

text

  • color — cmyk, hex, hsl, rgb
  • contact — email, phone
  • name — handle, organization, person, place
  • postal — full, po_box, street
  • text — label, literal, long, serialized, title
  • web — domain, ip, mac, url

unknown

  • unknown — malformed, mixed, unclassified

The detection kind

match_kind records how a semantic type is recognized from values — which is also what decides whether a column can be typed from its contents at all.

match_kind rows
genome 3
lexicon 10
mask 48
mask+lexicon 7
none 16
shape 12
match_kind recognized by examples
genome a tolerant multi-format parser calendar, timestamp, clock
mask a regex / format mask (often checksum-validated) ein, isbn, phone, usd
lexicon membership in a controlled vocabulary us_state, iso_country, first_name
mask+lexicon a shape gate, then a vocabulary check person (name-shaped and in the gazetteer)
shape a numeric distribution count, ratio, probability
none not value-detectable; only metadata can assert it record keys, free text, unknown

none-kind types are the reason some columns can never be pinned from values alone: a surrogate record key is just an integer, and free text is just text. Those are asserted by context (a column name, a data dictionary), not by guess_data_type().

The recipe: raw → stable → import

Four columns encode how a raw column is turned into a canonical, analysis-ready form. They use the formex expression syntax ({{ ... }}); the Formex vignette is the full guide.

column holds example
data_format the mask the raw file matches {{ mmddyyyy }}, {{ [strip:$,][dec:.2] }}
raw_to_stable_transform a lossless rewrite to canonical form {{ as_mmddyyyy }}, {{ as_usd }}, lookup:usps
stable_format what a stabilized value looks like 2019-03-15, CA
stable_import_rule how to read the stable column into its type {{ as_yyyymmdd }}, {{ as_integer }}

A few real rows, straight from the ontology:

semantic_type format_label match_kind data_format raw_to_stable_transform stable_format
calendar calendar genome {{ mmddyyyy }} {{ as_mmddyyyy }} 2019-03-15 ;; 2019-03-15
administrative ein mask {{ gov:ein }} {{ as_ein }} 12-3456789
usd usd mask {{ [strip:$,][range:-Inf,Inf][dec:.2] }} {{ as_usd }} {{ as_usd }} -45.00 ;; 2300.00 ;; 17298.00
person first_name lexicon {{ lexicon:given_name }} lookup:given given_name
count count shape {{ [range:0,Inf][dec:.0] }} {{ as_integer }} {{ as_integer }} 0 ;; 1 ;; 42

The split has a purpose: push as much as possible into the lossless reformat (raw_to_stable_transform), which every downstream tool benefits from, and reserve stable_import_rule for the genuinely schema-dependent step of coercing a value into a type a plain CSV reader cannot infer (a ZIP that must stay a categorical, an EIN that must stay an identifier).

Metadata: units, validation, lifecycle

The remaining columns are documentation the engine carries but does not parse:

  • dd_data_unit — an interpretive unit an analyst needs but a type does not (USD, kg, EPSG:4326). It is proposed only when the semantic type declares one. Crucially it does not carry temporal grain: a date’s grain (calendar vs month vs day-of-week) selects the render graphic, so it lives in semantic_type, not in a unit.
  • validation, default_storage, short_desc / detail — the human-facing description, the storage class a stabilized value round-trips to, and the checks a value should pass.
  • implemented — whether a value-level detector/recipe is wired up yet, so the ontology can name a type before its machinery exists.
  • version_added / version_deprecated / superseded_by — lifecycle. Rows are deprecated, never deleted, so old labels remain resolvable.

How the engine uses the ontology

guess_data_type() anchors a column to these coordinates. The $route record is the ontology path it resolved to, only as deep as it is confident:

r <- guess_data_type(c("03/15/2019", "12/31/2020", "01/01/2021"))$route
r[c("data_type", "semantic_family", "semantic_type", "format_label", "match_kind", "depth")]
#> $data_type
#> [1] "temporal"
#> 
#> $semantic_family
#> [1] "date"
#> 
#> $semantic_type
#> [1] "calendar"
#> 
#> $format_label
#> [1] "calendar"
#> 
#> $match_kind
#> [1] "genome"
#> 
#> $depth
#> [1] 4

fx_stabilize() looks up the recipe for a (semantic_type, format_label) pair and runs it, returning the stable values plus the format mask and import rule from that row:

fx_stabilize(c("California", "TX", "Ohio"), "geographic", "us_state")[
  c("stable", "stable_format", "import_rule")]
#> $stable
#> [1] "CA" "TX" "OH"
#> 
#> $stable_format
#> [1] "usps_state"
#> 
#> $import_rule
#> [1] "{{ as_factor }}"

Because both functions read the same fx_ontology(), a column typed by guess_data_type() can be handed straight to fx_stabilize() using the semantic_type and format_label it returned.
